Hamlet, Prince of Denmark, seeks revenge against his uncle Claudius, who has murdered King Hamlet and seized the throne, marrying Gertrude. Haunted by his father's ghost, Hamlet feigns madness to investigate, while contemplating life and death in his famous "To be, or not to be" soliloquy. His indecision leads to the deaths of Polonius, Ophelia (who drowns), and Laertes, who challenges Hamlet to a fatal duel. Mortally wounded, Hamlet kills Claudius and dies, restoring order with Fortinbras claiming the throne.

The play follows Prince Hamlet of Denmark, who is grief-stricken after his father's death and his mother Gertrude's hasty remarriage to his uncle Claudius. When the ghost of the late king reveals that Claudius murdered him to seize the throne and marry Gertrude, Hamlet vows revenge. To test Claudius's guilt, Hamlet feigns madness and stages a play reenacting the murder. Claudius's guilty reaction confirms the truth. Hamlet then delays killing Claudius, contemplating existential questions and mistreating Ophelia, which contributes to her madness and death. A series of fatal events unfolds: Hamlet kills Polonius by mistake, Ophelia drowns, and Laertes returns to challenge Hamlet to a fencing match. Claudius plots to kill Hamlet with a poisoned sword and poisoned drink. In the climactic duel, both are wounded by the poisoned blade, Gertrude drinks the poisoned wine and dies, and Hamlet finally kills Claudius. Mortally wounded, Hamlet names Fortinbras as his successor and dies, restoring order to the kingdom.
